stories.headline: Quest v72 update: faster hand tracking, glance-to-connect PC
stories.subtitle: Look at a PC and tap Connect for Remote Desktop; more stable hand cursor and passthrough keyboard tracking. The update is rolling out now to Quest headsets.

stories.headline: Gen 3 in stores at $449; camera-free Audio ships Oct 13
stories.subtitle: Gen 3 adds Aviator, Zena, a slimmer build and longer battery at $449; the $349 camera-free Audio line — no camera at all, for the privacy-conscious — ships Oct 13.

stories.headline: Norway proposes temporary ban on AI smart glasses
stories.subtitle: Norway's government proposed restricting camera-equipped glasses — including Ray-Ban and Oakley Meta models — in schools, hospitals, gyms, museums, parks and public events over covert-recording fears. Not a blanket ban; it buys time to write longer-term rules.

stories.headline: Meta sells refurbished Gen 1 glasses from $179–$239
stories.subtitle: Meta's refurbished store lists Gen 1 Wayfarer, Headliner and Skyler frames from $179–$239 with a one-year warranty; new Gen 1s start at $224. For customers hunting the cheapest way into Meta's glasses, this is the floor.

stories.headline: ESPN brings live college football to Quest in immersive 180°
stories.subtitle: Meta is partnering with ESPN to stream select live 180° college football games through Quest's TV app, and promised 100+ live sporting events next year. One more demo-friendly answer for customers asking what Quest is good for.
